cities.base: Yosemite Valley Lodge or Half Dome Village, both on the valley floor within walking distance of the main trailheads
cities.name: Yosemite Valley

cities.base: Tuolumne Meadows Lodge tent cabins, the only beds up here and right on the meadow
cities.name: Tuolumne Meadows

cities.base: Day trip only, shuttle required in peak summer
cities.name: Mariposa Grove

places.name: Lower Yosemite Fall Trail
places.note: Crowded but the payoff is immediate; best in spring when the fall is actually running.

places.name: Vernal Fall / Mist Trail
places.note: Slick granite steps soaked in spray; worth the wet shoes. In winter the upper Mist Trail steps ice over, so turn back at the footbridge if they are glazed.

places.name: Four Mile Trail to Glacier Point
places.note: Genuinely strenuous, 6-8 hours; skip if anyone in the group isn't a real hiker. It tops out at Glacier Point, whose road runs late May to October or November, and winter closures of the trail are common, so call 209-372-0200.

places.name: Sentinel Beach
places.note: A quiet stretch of the Merced to cool off after a hike.

places.name: The Ahwahnee Dining Room
places.note: Dinner is a 5-course prix fixe at $95 (7 courses $125, wine pairing $40 more), and the room is the reason to go once. Book on OpenTable; dinner means long pants and a collared shirt, no shorts or caps. Breakfast 07:00 to 10:00, lunch 11:30 to 14:00.

places.name: Lembert Dome
places.note: Quiet, high, cold at night even in July. Tioga Road runs roughly late May or June to October or November, so check it has not closed for snow.

places.name: Cathedral Lakes Trail
places.note: Fewer people than anything in the valley; this is the day people remember. Tioga Road runs roughly late May or June to October or November, so check it has not closed for snow.

places.name: Tenaya Lake
places.note: Cold swim, good for breaking up the drive. Tioga Road runs roughly late May or June to October or November, so check it has not closed for snow.

places.name: Mariposa Grove
places.note: The big trees are real; go early. The grove road is closed to cars from late November to at least April 1 and the shuttle stops after Nov 30, so in winter you walk 2 miles in by the Washburn Trail or the road.

places.name: Tunnel View
places.note: The classic shot of Half Dome, El Capitan and Bridalveil Fall from one pullout on the Wawona Road, free beyond the $35 park entry per car. The lot fills fast; five minutes is enough, so stop on the drive in or out.

places.name: El Capitan Meadow
places.note: Flat meadow looking straight up the 3000-foot granite face, free beyond park entry. Bring binoculars in spring or fall to spot climbers on the wall; no trail, just a pull-off and a walk into the grass.

places.name: Mirror Lake Trail
places.note: Easy flat path along Tenaya Creek to a seasonal pool that reflects Half Dome, real lake only in spring runoff, a dry meadow of cobbles by August. Good low-effort option if legs are tired from the day before.

places.name: Village Store, Yosemite Village
places.note: The only real grocery store on the valley floor. Stock up here for the cheap self-catered days rather than paying lodge restaurant prices, gets picked over by evening in peak season.

places.name: Degnan's Kitchen
places.note: Fast sandwiches and coffee in Yosemite Village, breakfast 07:00 to 11:00 and lunch 11:30 to 18:00, open all year. Not memorable food, just efficient; the price here is a rough lunch-with-drink figure, so check the price.

places.name: Glacier Point Road (drive-up option)
places.note: Skip driving up separately since day 3 reaches the same point on foot via Four Mile Trail. The road typically opens late May and closes in October or November for snow, becoming a ski route, so it is likely shut now.

places.name: Cook's Meadow Loop
places.note: Flat boardwalk loop with open views of Half Dome, Yosemite Falls, and Sentinel Rock all from one meadow. Good easy evening walk after a hard hiking day, especially near sunset.

places.name: Happy Isles Nature Center
places.note: Small nature center at the start of the Mist Trail, a five-minute stop while gearing up for Vernal Fall. The Happy Isles Art and Nature Center opens April through October only, so it is closed now; the trail area stays open.

places.name: Tuolumne Meadows Visitor Center
places.note: NPS runs this as the Tuolumne Meadows Wilderness Center, for trail conditions and permits, open roughly late May to mid October, so it is closed now. Not a destination on its own; stop before Lembert Dome.

places.name: Soda Springs and Parsons Memorial Lodge
places.note: Flat 1.5 mile round trip through the meadow to carbonated springs and a stone lodge. Parsons Memorial Lodge opens late June to early September only, so it is closed now, and Tioga Road shuts for snow in October or November.

places.name: Elizabeth Lake Trail
places.note: 4.6 mile round trip from the campground, about 800 ft gain, 3-4 hrs, to a subalpine lake below Unicorn Peak; the shorter day than Cathedral Lakes. Tioga Road runs roughly late May or June to October or November, so check it has not closed for snow.

places.name: Mono Pass Trail
places.note: 7.4 mile round trip, 900 ft gain, 4 hrs, with old mining cabins near the pass and fewer people than Cathedral Lakes. Tioga Road runs roughly late May or June to October or November, so check it has not closed for snow.

places.name: Tuolumne Meadows Grill
places.note: Walk-up breakfast to 11:00, then burgers from 11:15, by the store. Open May 30 to Sep 20 in 2026, so closed now; the price here is not confirmed, so check the price.

places.name: Tuolumne Meadows Lodge Dining Tent
places.note: Breakfast and a sit-down dinner in a canvas tent, dinner reservations required on 209-372-8413. Open June 5 to Sep 13 in 2026, so closed now; the price here is not confirmed, so check the price.

places.name: Olmsted Point
places.note: Pullout on Tioga Road with a view down Tenaya Canyon to the back of Half Dome, five minutes from the lot. Tioga Road runs roughly late May or June to October or November, so check it has not closed for snow.

places.name: Pothole Dome
places.note: Short scramble up the granite slabs of a dome at the west end of the meadow, no trail. Good sunset spot that most people drive past. Tioga Road runs roughly late May or June to October or November, so check it has not closed for snow.

places.name: Mariposa Grove Trail (Big Trees Loop)
places.note: Easy paved loop past the first cluster of sequoias, including the Fallen Monarch. Good option if you only have an hour and don't want the climb to Mariposa Grove Trail's upper loop.

places.name: Grizzly Giant
places.note: One of the largest and oldest sequoias in the grove, over 1,800 years old. Short walk from the entrance, always crowded but it's the one everyone wants to see.

places.name: California Tunnel Tree
places.note: Cut in 1895 so carriages (and later cars) could drive through, still standing and walkable. Right next to Grizzly Giant, worth the two minute detour.

places.name: Mariposa Grove Museum
places.note: A 1930 log cabin, rebuilt in 1980 and on the National Register since 1978, at the top of the upper grove with small sequoia exhibits. Hours vary, check, and check the price; after Nov 30 there is no shuttle, so it is a long walk in.

places.name: Mariposa Grove Welcome Plaza Shuttle Stop
places.note: Free shuttle to the grove: 08:00 to 15:30 in November, to 17:00 Sep 24 to Oct 31, to 19:00 May 3 to Sep 23. None from Dec 1 to at least Apr 15, when the road is shut to cars and you walk the 2 miles in.

places.name: Wawona Meadow Loop
places.note: Flat 3.5 mile loop around an open meadow near the Wawona Hotel, good for stretching legs after the grove without any real elevation gain. Quiet, almost nobody does it.

places.name: The Mountain Room
places.note: Dinner only, 17:00 to 21:00 all year, with Yosemite Falls outside the windows. The Beast Burger is $35, mains on the fall and winter menu run $28 to $72, starters $6 to $20.

places.name: Base Camp Eatery
places.note: Food court with a Starbucks, open all year: breakfast 07:00 to 10:30, then lunch and dinner to 20:00, though listings disagree, so hours vary, check. Chicken strips and fries run about $18, breakfast for two nearly $40.

places.name: Curry Village Pizza Deck
places.note: Pizza on a deck below Glacier Point, 12:00 to 21:00; a medium El Capitan is $28.50 and does two, smalls $18.75 to $24. Open January to November and holidays, so open now but closed in December apart from the holidays.

places.name: Yosemite Valley Visitor Center
places.note: First stop for road and trail conditions, open all year 09:00 to 17:00 and free beyond park entry. Ranger programs, the park film and a bookstore; 30 minutes.

places.name: Yosemite Museum and Indian Village of Ahwahnee
places.note: Miwok and Paiute history since 1850, with beadwork and basket demonstrations at set times, free; the rebuilt village of Ahwahnee behind it is always open. Hours come from a third party, so call 209-372-0200.

places.name: The Ansel Adams Gallery
places.note: Gallery and shop with Ansel Adams prints, contemporary photographers, books and crafts, listed by NPS among the Valley's historic sites. Free to browse, 10:00 to 17:00 daily.

places.name: Yosemite Valley Chapel
places.note: Built in 1879 to a Carpenter Gothic design by Charles Geddes and moved here in 1901, the oldest structure in the Valley and on the National Register since 1973. The interior opens for Sunday services from 09:15; free.

places.name: Yosemite Conservation Heritage Center (LeConte Memorial Lodge)
places.note: The Valley's first public visitor centre, now a National Historic Landmark run by the Sierra Club with a library and evening programs. Wed to Sun 10:00 to 16:00, May to September only, so closed now; no fee listed, check the price.

places.name: Bridalveil Fall
places.note: A short easy walk to the foot of the fall, strongest in spring, free beyond park entry and on a road open all year. Expect mist and slippery rock, and the trail can close for works.

places.name: Pioneer Yosemite History Center
places.note: Park buildings moved to Wawona in the 1950s and 60s: the Chinese Laundry, a homestead cabin, Degnan's Bakery, the Wells Fargo office and a covered bridge on the National Register. Grounds open all year, no fee beyond park entry; interiors and wagon rides are summer only.
places.neighborhood: Wawona, 24 km south of the Valley

places.name: Whoa Nellie Deli
places.note: A deli inside the Lee Vining gas station, 20 km east of Tioga Pass: fish tacos and lobster taquitos about $15.50, live music Thursday and Sunday in summer. Open about May to October, so closed now until late April.

outings.why: An easy, crowded, immediate payoff walk to the base of the fall, best when it's actually running in spring.
outings.name: Lower Yosemite Fall

outings.why: Slick granite steps soaked in spray, moderate but genuinely wet, worth ruining a pair of shoes for.
outings.name: Vernal Fall via the Mist Trail

outings.why: A real climb, 9.6 miles round trip, 6-8 hours, with the payoff of a real view of Half Dome; skip it if anyone in the group isn't a real hiker.
outings.name: Four Mile Trail to Glacier Point
outings.fallback: Lower Yosemite Fall walk if weather or fitness rules it out

outings.why: A 1.5 hour drive up to the high country followed by a quiet walk around the dome; the road only runs roughly June to October, so check conditions before booking around it.
outings.name: Tioga Road drive and Lembert Dome walk

outings.why: Seven miles round trip with far fewer people than anything in the valley; the day that makes people say Tuolumne was the better half of the trip.
outings.name: Cathedral Lakes Trail

outings.why: A cold swim that breaks up the long drive back down through the valley.
outings.name: Tenaya Lake swim

outings.why: The giant sequoias are real, but parking is a fight and shuttle access is required in peak summer, so go early.
outings.name: Mariposa Grove
outings.season: Year-round, shuttle required in peak summer

destination.name: Yosemite National Park
destination.pitch: A week of granite, waterfalls, and real hiking, split between the crowded valley floor and the quieter, colder high country at Tuolumne.
destination.caveat: Lodging inside the park sells out six to twelve months ahead, and the fallback of commuting in from outside eats hours you don't have on a 7-day trip; wildfire smoke in August-September can close trails or ruin the views with no warning. Put together for you just now from a live search, so check anything you're pinning the trip on.

because.nature: Granite domes, giant sequoias, and waterfalls running at full force in spring.
because.adventure: Four Mile Trail to Glacier Point and the Mist Trail are real climbs with real exposure, not strolls.
because.relaxation: Sentinel Beach and Tenaya Lake give you a cold swim to break up the hiking.
because.exploration: Tuolumne Meadows and Cathedral Lakes see a fraction of the valley's crowds.
